name: Mars
lede: A cold desert world of giant volcanoes, canyon systems, and rovers still working the surface.

landmark.label: Olympus Mons
landmark.blurb: The tallest known volcano in the solar system — a shield about 22 km high and hundreds of kilometers across.

missions.name: Viking 1 & 2
missions.note: First successful soft landings with imaging and surface experiments.

missions.name: Curiosity
missions.note: Gale crater rover studying habitability and organic chemistry.

missions.name: Perseverance
missions.note: Jezero crater sample caching for a future Mars Sample Return.

researchNotes: A Martian day (sol) is about 24 hours 40 minutes. Axial tilt near Earth's gives seasons, though the year lasts nearly two Earth years.
Olympus Mons and the Tharsis volcanoes dwarf terrestrial peaks. Valles Marineris stretches thousands of kilometers as a vast canyon system.
Two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, are irregular and likely captured asteroids. Dust storms can grow planet-wide and alter surface temperatures.
folklore: Canal myths from early telescopes and war-of-the-worlds fiction are cultural history — spacecraft show dry channels carved by ancient water, not engineering.
carlFocus: Highlight Olympus Mons, sols vs Earth days, Viking-to-Perseverance heritage, and clear canal myth from geology.
